title: Console backend: unit economics query API endpoints (time series + breakdowns)
creator: Dylan Brooks
description:
Build the Console backend endpoints powering the internal Unit Economics dashboard. Endpoints must support time series and breakdown queries for the canonical metric (blended $/1M output tokens) with drilldowns by model/version/quantization profile, region, and customer tier. Include pagination, caching strategy, and guardrails for performance/cardinality.

Background
- Data is produced by the hourly unit economics aggregation job (ENG-8426) into warehouse materialized views.
- We need low-latency dashboard queries with predictable load on the warehouse and clear semantics around freshness.
- Access is internal-only behind feature flag + RBAC (ENG-8434).

API surface (internal)
1) GET /api/internal/unit-economics/v1/timeseries
- Purpose: chart + comparisons over time.
- Params:
  - start (ISO8601, inclusive)
  - end (ISO8601, exclusive)
  - granularity: hour | day (default: day; hour allowed up to 14d range)
  - metric: blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens (v1 only; keep extensible)
  - filters (all optional):
    - model (canonical model_id)
    - model_version (runtime model build/version string)
    - quantization_profile (allowed-value enum; see ENG-8425)
    - region (canonical region)
    - customer_tier (self_serve | dedicated | private | enterprise)
    - streaming (true|false)
- Response (per bucket):
  - ts
  - cost_usd (numerator)
  - output_tokens (denominator)
  - blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens
  - coverage/quality fields: missing_dimension_rate, late_data_hours (for confidence indicator wiring)

2) GET /api/internal/unit-economics/v1/breakdown
- Purpose: top tables + drilldown slices (group-by one dimension, optionally filtered by others).
- Params:
  - start/end
  - group_by: model | model_version | quantization_profile | region | customer_tier
  - metric: blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens
  - limit (default 25, max 200)
  - cursor (opaque; for pagination)
  - sort: cost_per_1m_desc | cost_per_1m_asc | output_tokens_desc | cost_usd_desc
  - filters: same as timeseries
- Response:
  - rows: [{key, display_name, cost_usd, output_tokens, blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens, share_of_tokens, share_of_cost}]
  - next_cursor
  - totals: total_cost_usd, total_output_tokens, total_blended_cost_per_1m (note: totals computed from sums; not average of row metrics)

3) GET /api/internal/unit-economics/v1/topn (thin wrapper)
- Purpose: common dashboard call for “Top N by blended cost” with sane defaults.
- Params:
  - start/end
  - dimension (same as group_by)
  - n (default 10, max 50)
  - filters: same as above
- Response: same shape as breakdown, without cursor.

Implementation notes
- Data source: warehouse views/materializations from ENG-8426. We should avoid dynamic SQL; use a fixed set of parameterized queries per (granularity x group_by) and push filters via safe bindings.
- Dimension normalization:
  - Use canonical region mapping (ENG-8424) and canonical model identifiers (ENG-8422).
  - Customer tier values must match derivation logic (ENG-8423).
- Performance requirements:
  - P50 < 300ms / P95 < 1.2s for typical dashboard ranges (7d/day granularity, breakdown limit 25).
  - No query should scan raw request-level metering tables.
  - Enforce reasonable limits: day granularity up to 400d, hour granularity up to 14d.
- Pagination:
  - Use cursor-based pagination for breakdown endpoint.
  - Cursor should encode (sort_key, tie_breaker_key) to keep stable ordering across pages.
- Caching plan (server-side)
  - Add a request cache layer keyed by: endpoint + normalized params + authz scope + rate_card_version (if applicable).
  - Cache store: Redis (shared Console backend cache).
  - TTL policy:
    - Ranges ending within the last 6 hours: TTL 60s (expect late-arriving data/backfills)
    - Ranges ending 6h–48h ago: TTL 5m
    - Ranges ending >48h ago: TTL 30m
  - Cache stampede protection: single-flight per cache key.
  - Separate “finance view” caching to align with Finance expectations (see notes below).
- Freshness semantics
  - Response should include data_freshness_lag_minutes and last_successful_aggregation_hour so the UI can show a freshness indicator.
  - Do not silently drop unknown dimension values; bucket as "unknown" and include unknown_* counts.
- Access control + audit
  - All routes are internal-only behind the unit_economics_dashboard feature flag.
  - Require RBAC permission: console.internal_unit_economics.read.
  - Audit log: record viewer, time range, group_by, filters (redacted), and endpoint.
- Privacy/security
  - No customer_id or org-level identifiers in response.
  - Filters must not accept raw customer_id (explicitly out of scope for v1; see privacy thread).
  - Ensure parameters cannot cause unbounded cardinality (quantization_profile is allowlisted).

Open questions / follow-ups
- Do we need a stable “rate_card_version” parameter for Finance reporting snapshots, or do we always use the current versioned rate card joined by effective_date? (Finance leaning: versioned, with clear effective ranges.)
- How do we expose a confidence indicator without giving a false sense of precision? (Likely: show missing_dimension_rate + data lag; UI decides.)

Acceptance criteria
- Endpoints above implemented and wired to the internal dashboard UI.
- Cursor pagination works and is stable under typical refresh patterns.
- Caching reduces warehouse load (verify via query counts/latency before vs after; attach graphs in final update).
- RBAC + feature flag enforced; security review sign-off for audit logging/redaction.
- Documented in internal Console API docs with example requests/responses and known limitations.

References
- PRD: Internal Unit Economics Dashboard v1
- UX spec: Unit economics dashboard drilldown UX
- Telemetry standards: token-metering dimensions and cardinality
- Related implementation PR: pr-19374-unit-economics-query-api-endpoints (link in comments)
comments: 2025-01-10 (Chloe Martin): Kicked off with Felix + Mei. We’ll implement timeseries + breakdown first; topN can be a thin wrapper. Waiting on final schema names from ENG-8426 to avoid churn.

2025-01-16 (Felix Schneider): Proposed query contract: group_by + filters + limit/cursor. Added guardrails: hour granularity max 14d and breakdown max 200 rows. Sharing draft with Product/Finance for sanity check.

2025-01-22 (Laura Bennett): Finance request: a visible freshness indicator + ability to run QTD without the dashboard timing out. Also asked that totals are computed from summed numerator/denominator (not averaging per-row blended metrics).

2025-01-27 (Allison Grant): Please add cache stampede protection and include last_successful_aggregation_hour in the payload so SRE can correlate incidents. Also ensure we don’t add any customer-identifying fields in responses.

2025-02-03 (Marcus Lin): Security review note: audit logs must not include free-form filter values that could contain identifiers. Please log filter keys only, and normalize/validate values before logging.

2025-02-07 (Chloe Martin): Implemented endpoints behind feature flag + RBAC check. Added response fields: data_freshness_lag_minutes, last_successful_aggregation_hour, missing_dimension_rate. Cursor pagination uses (sort_metric, key) for stability.
2025-02-11 (Mei Lin): Warehouse view performance looks OK for 7d/day. Hour granularity over 30d is too slow; we’re enforcing 14d limit server-side. ENG-8431 will optimize partitions/materializations.

2025-02-14 (Chloe Martin): Added Redis caching with TTL tiers (1m/5m/30m) and single-flight per key. Verified cache hit rate ~70% for dogfood traffic; warehouse query count dropped materially. Ready for final review.
2025-02-19 (Chloe Martin): Shipped in pr-19374. UI wired in ENG-8428. Follow-up created to add optional rate_card_version parameter once Finance finalizes snapshot requirements.
